body:
Also reproducible in v4.5.beta6.official [d5ad0556a]

What I believe is an additional consequence of this bug, and how I experienced it, is that: if a `RESET` animation contains an animation track (in my case a default character pose), calling `play("RESET")` **will not trigger the embedded animation**, despite it working when changing animations in the animation editor UI.

This can be demonstrated in the MRP by:

1. Disable the three existing tracks in `CutsceneAnimations`'s RESET animation;
2. Add the `CharacterAnimations`'s "idle_front" animation to `CutsceneAnimations`'s RESET;
3. Use the `CutsceneAnimations.current_animation` property to play either of the cutscene tracks, and then the RESET track;
4. ⚠️ Notice that the character is still facing sideways, and not face-on!
5. Note that if you subsequently use `current_animation` to RESET _again_, the (first frame of) the sub-animation *will* take effect!

A workaround I found for this particular manifestation is to `seek` immediately after `play`, eg:
```gdscript
func reset() -> void:
    play("RESET")
    seek(0.001)
```

I've since learned this side note on the `AnimationPlayer.play(..)` docs ([here](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_animationplayer.html#class-animationplayer-method-play)):
> **Note:** The animation will be updated the next time the **AnimationPlayer** is processed. If other variables are updated at the same time this is called, they may be updated too early. To perform the update immediately, call `advance(0)`.

I believe this issue is a side effect of this requirement, or at least related to it. ~~I have a theory that a more robust workaround might be to add a function call track for calling `advance(0)` any time the animation changes, or adding a callback to `animation_changed` signal for doing that, but haven't had the time to test if either of these work.~~

_EDIT: scratch that, didn't seem to work._

Finally found the time and energy to take another look at this. Toyed around with the MRP a bit more, and debunked my earlier theory about calling `advance(0)` via a method call track. However, while trying to get that workaround to work, I noticed that changing `callback_process_mode` to `ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_PHYSICS` seems to mitigate the issue. I was 99% sure I've tried this before, but now I couldn't get the animation to break when process mode is set to _Physics_. Doing this likely has a lot of subtle implications, as presumably, the animation is now processed _a lot_ more often, in comparison to when it is advanced during the process frames. E.g. if used for a ton of animated sprites, this could have performance implications.

Added some debug logging to figure out the tick order of the animation players. I wanted to figure out if the `CharacterAnimations` (or `player2`) is ticked before or after the `CutsceneAnimations` swaps its animation via the animation playback track. As a result, I learned that the `CharacterAnimations` does not receive `NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS` **at all on the tick the animation changes**. ...this led to another "eureka!" -moment: the gap between the animation playback keyframes in the MRP is significant. The issue does not occur if there is no gap between the played animations. Seems that the `AnimationPlayer`/`AnimationMixer` implementations disable ticking via `set_process_internal(false)` when there is no animation playing. Due to this, during the tick when the new animation is played, iff there was no animation playing during the previous tick, the animation player will not receive `NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS`, and will not call `_process_animation` for that tick, at all. I assume this is the "why" for the `advance(0)` hint in the docs. However, with animation playback tracks, not calling the `_process_animation` means that the animation playback track changes have a single tick delay. This isn't an issue by-itself, but becomes quite awkward, when viewed from the point of view of the animation timeline, as all e.g. `TrackType::TYPE_VALUE` tracks apply the keyframes immediately. Furthermore, as there is no way of consistently/reliably delay the other track types by a single frame in situations where framerates fluctuate, the animation playback tracks are effectively incompatible (timing-wise) with all other animation track types. ### Summary of the issue: To summarize, my best understanding of the issue as of now is that: 1. `AnimationPlayer` does not receive `NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS` when there is no animation playing. This is perfectly reasonable, as there is no reason run processing when nothing is playing. 2. When the animation playback track hits a new keyframe, it calls `player2->play(..)` (with `player2` being the animation player targeted by the track). 3. If `player2` is not currently playing any animations, as per 1., it will not process, at all, until next process tick. 4. Nothing special is done to advance the animation on `player2` immediately (!!) 5. Therefore, `player2->_process_animation(..)` will not be called until the next process tick. As a frame is rendered in the meantime, animation playback tracks have a single frame delay, in comparison to other track types. For a real fix, the `player2` should somehow be forced to process its animations after the `player2->play(..)`. Just calling `player2->advance(0)` or `player2->_process_animation(0)` achieves this, but at least in theory, I believe it is prone to e.g. infinite loops. Not sure how such "recursive" call to `_process_animation` from (effectively) within another `_process_animation` would interact in more complex animation blending situations, either. ### Some workarounds: 1. Manually set the `animation` and `frame` to the start of the new animation via a property track, at the same time the animation playback track changes animations. This is cumbersome, and adds unnecessary noise to the animation editor. 2. Changing the callback process mode from _"Idle"_ to _"Physics"_ makes it somewhat unlikely that the animation change is processed during the exact physics tick that ends up rendered, mitigating the issue. This is not a real fix, as from what I can tell, the issue can still rarely occur, although I wasn't able to confirm this in-editor. 3. Connect a **deferred** callback, calling `advance(0)` to the `current_animation_changed` on the animation player targeted by the animation playback track (as described [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104046#issuecomment-3498632628)). This forces the animation to auto-advance at the end of the frame any time the animation changes, which seemed to reliably fix the issue.

The more I stare at the code, the less I see ways of wiggling out of just requesting the targeted animation player to process immediately. Anything more refined would likely either require non-trivial amount refactoring or adding quite unpleasant amounts of complexity on top of a system that is quite complex beast already.

Opened a draft PR to better communicate my findings and thoughts on the naive fix.

I'm not sure if I've been experiencing a different issue, or if its because I'm doing it with a skelatal 3d model, but are you sure its a single frame delay? In my current project, I'm dealing with about half a second of delay (and I'm getting more than 2 FPS), and my previous project I had similar issues with Animation Playback Track, having to move it back quite a lot for not to show something incorrect, and I can't be sure if it always works when doing that.
My issue only seems to happen in the game itself, in the editor when played from the Animation timeline panel it works without issue.
